transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I keep getting these sudden, vivid memories of the train crash that pop into my head and completely derail whatever I’m doing. It happened a little over two years ago, and I've realized I just can't "power through" them on my own anymore.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid places, situations, or even thoughts and conversations that remind you of the train crash?

Yes, I’ve basically built my whole life around avoiding anything to do with trains. I’ll drive an extra hour in traffic instead of taking the Metro-North, and I refuse to book client meetings if they are near a station. I even have to change the TV channel if a subway scene comes on because my chest starts tightening just from the sound of it.
Since the crash, have you noticed changes in your sleep, or do you find yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or unusually irritable?

Yes, all of those have become major issues for me. I lie awake wired until 2 or 3 AM tensing for an impact, and when I do sleep, I'm constantly jerked awake by awful train nightmares. I'm also always on edge, flinching at loud noises and scanning every room, and my fuse is so short now that I keep snapping at my boyfriend and coworkers over the smallest things.
Since the accident, have you noticed any persistent negative changes in your thoughts or mood, such as feeling detached from loved ones or struggling to feel positive emotions?

My outlook on everything has definitely taken a really dark turn, and I constantly feel like the world is just a rigged game where disaster can strike out of nowhere. I've lost all confidence in my own competence and feel like I can't even trust my own commute. I'm also plagued by this endless self-blame, constantly thinking that if I hadn't stayed late at work that night or had somehow pulled the emergency brake, I could have prevented the whole thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (ICD-10: F43.1). They experienced a qualifying traumatic event (a train crash two years ago) and present with persistent intrusive symptoms (vivid memories, nightmares, physiological reactivity to reminders), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (avoiding trains, stations, and media depictions), negative alterations in cognitions and mood (pervasive negative beliefs, self-blame), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (insomnia, hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, and irritability). Symptoms have persisted for over two years and cause significant functional impairment in their professional and personal life.
